plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid (which is what you'd pay), and truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Since this is a single round with no repeated learning needed, and the format matches standard Vickrey auction rules, I will bid exactly my value of $33 to ensure optimal expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying only that second-highest bid, and never overpay. Bidding above value risks winning at a price above your value (loss), while bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single-round game with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my value of $32 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks negative profit and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With a value of $41, I should bid exactly $41 to maximize expected profit.
